selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: At the start of this passage, what question is being asked about all things?
questions.answer: Whether all created things, in their own way, say Allah’s name.

questions.question: In the example, why would a single person driving a town’s people seem impossible by himself?
questions.answer: Because that work is too great for one person alone.

questions.question: In the same way, whose strength is behind the work of creation?
questions.answer: Allah’s strength.

questions.question: What big thing comes from those tiny things?
questions.answer: Large trees.

questions.question: What do trees provide that shows mercy?
questions.answer: Food and benefits for people.

questions.question: Which animals in the passage are examples of Allah’s provision?
questions.answer: Cows, camels, sheep, and goats.

questions.question: What does this show about hard things like rock and dirt?
questions.answer: They are under Allah’s command.

questions.question: What surprising job do very soft roots do?
questions.answer: They enter and pass through hard rock and earth.

questions.question: What two things are said to challenge the ideas of naturalist thinkers?
questions.answer: Roots breaking through rock and leaves staying moist in heat.

questions.question: What is the big lesson from roots, leaves, rock, and heat together?
questions.answer: Everything obeys Allah.

questions.question: What main idea is answered with “Yes, it is so”?
questions.answer: That all things show, in their own way, that they act with Allah’s name.

questions.question: What picture is given to help answer that question?
questions.answer: A lone man making a whole town’s people move and work.

questions.question: How does this help us understand the world?
questions.answer: It shows that created things do their work with Allah’s power.

questions.question: What does the passage say trees are doing for us?
questions.answer: Bringing us gifts from Allah’s mercy.

questions.question: What giant living things come from them?
questions.answer: Trees.

questions.question: Which four animals are called blessed in the passage?
questions.answer: Cows, camels, sheep, and goats.

questions.question: What other weak-looking part of a plant is mentioned besides roots?
questions.answer: Thin green leaves.

questions.question: What does the passage say about tiny roots?
questions.answer: They are soft, but they still push through rock and soil.

questions.question: What claim about nature is being pushed back against?
questions.answer: The idea that nature works by itself without Allah.

questions.question: What is being explained through examples in this passage?
questions.answer: That all things work in Allah’s name.

questions.question: In that example, who is the man acting for?
questions.answer: He is acting for the government and under the king’s power.

questions.question: What is the matching truth about the world?
questions.answer: All things act by Allah’s permission and power.

questions.question: What can we learn from a tiny seed making a giant tree?
questions.answer: Allah gives great power to small things.

questions.question: What kinds of animals are mentioned as giving milk?
questions.answer: Cows, camels, sheep, and goats.
